capabilities: Study flashcards written as level-2 headings in any note or in .cards.md decks
Save each review as a hidden comment line under the card in its own note
Schedule reviews with FSRS-6 and configurable retention, learning steps and new-card limits
Open notes as decks from the file explorer, ribbon, status bar or commands on desktop and mobile
Provide an agent skill and checker script that teach AI agents to write decks in the format
extras: Works fully offline with no network requests, accounts or telemetry. Includes an agent skill (skills/plain-deck-flashcards) with a Node-based deck checker for AI agents such as Claude Code, and example decks including one from Designing Data-Intensive Applications. Development happens in a separate repository; contributions ship with the next release.
intentEvidence: Several Obsidian plugins let you study flashcards written in your notes.
problem: Other Obsidian flashcard plugins keep review progress in separate databases or device-specific files, so study progress does not sync naturally with the vault.

relations.evidence: The others also do things Plain Deck doesn't: Decks imports Anki collections
Spaced Repetition schedules whole notes for review
Scheduling is FSRS-6, the algorithm Anki uses

summary: Flashcard plugin that turns level-2 headings in notes into spaced-repetition cards (FSRS-6) and saves review progress inside the note itself.
